fixes.explanation: I get the thinking, since twenty and up would pull in a lot more men. But the LORD gives Moses and Aaron a window of thirty to fifty for this work (Numbers 4:3). Both ends of that window count, so a man who is fifty is still in. It's a window with two sides, and the LORD named both.

Counting is Moses and Aaron's job in this passage. The LORD tells them to take the census (Numbers 4:2), so the Kohathites are the ones being counted, not the ones doing the counting. The hauling comes later, once Aaron and his sons have covered the holy objects and the camp is ready to move (Numbers 4:15). Getting on the list is one thing, and lifting is another. I only count cookies, and I lose a few to my own mustache.

Shields and spears? Friend, I love the energy, but nobody here is marching off to battle. The Gershonites haul the curtains of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting with its covering of fine leather, and the courtyard curtains, plus the ropes and equipment (Numbers 4:25-26). It's heavy fabric and zero battle cries. The only thing getting swung around is a curtain, and I bet folding it still takes some fight.

Baskets and sacks would be easy to pack, and that's the trouble, because this load isn't. The Merarites carry the frames of the tabernacle with its crossbars, posts and bases (Numbers 4:31). They also carry the courtyard posts with their bases, tent pegs and ropes (Numbers 4:32). Somebody's whole job includes TENT PEGS. One peg rolls off and the whole crew is staring at the ground.

Not quite, friend. All three clans are counted, the Kohathites, the Gershonites and the Merarites, and the total comes to 8,580 (Numbers 4:46-48). Then verse 49 says each one was assigned his work and burden. So the assigning reaches every counted man, and one clan doesn't get all of it.

False, and verse 49 is why. After the count of 8,580, each man is given his own work and burden, so it reaches the Gershonites and the Merarites too (Numbers 4:46-49). Three clans, three sets of jobs, and nobody left standing around holding a clipboard. Even I'd have a task in that crowd, probably the one nobody else wanted.
